issues.body: `_workflow_job_key` still bounds the job with `(?=^  \S|\Z)`. A two-space comment satisfies that lookahead even though YAML ignores comment-only lines for mapping structure. Placing `  # keepalive controls` after the captured `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` and before `    if: false` truncates the block: `runs-on` supplies the positive control, while `if` incorrectly reads as absent, so the live row stays green although GitHub disables the job. The new `synthetic_job` contains only `    # if: ...`, a four-space comment, and does not test the round-3 boundary case.
issues.fix_hint: Make job-boundary detection skip comment-only lines while still refusing missing or ambiguous job definitions. Add the exact independent regression fixture: a two-space comment between `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` and a four-space `if: false`, and assert that the gate is still returned while the positive control occurs before the comment.
issues.title: A job-indented comment still hides subsequent job gates

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The round-3 major remains unchanged. `_workflow_job_key` still ends its capture at `(?=^  \S|\Z)`, so a valid two-space YAML comment is treated as the next job boundary. The added synthetic job retains only a four-space comment inside the job and therefore does not exercise the reported bypass. If a two-space comment follows `runs-on` and precedes `    if: false`, the positive control remains visible while the gate is truncated from the captured block; the production assertion consequently reports `(None, "ubuntu-latest")` and passes although the job is disabled. Because the same soundness defect remains at the same severity, progress is stagnant.
